book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Final trading time to settle all debt, yes?

indicators.note: to settle something is to sort it out and put it in order, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: A trader asks whether the closing bell is the moment to clear every debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The money words make 'settle all debt' read as finance; 'to settle' is the instruction to sort the letters of 'all debt, yes' into SELL-BY DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-by date is the last day a shop may offer the goods for sale, the end of their trading life.

clue.text: Put a stop to energetic game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to suppress or crush
second meaning: a fast racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the sport share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash a rumour or rebellion is to suppress it, and squash is a vigorous indoor racket sport.

clue.text: Advertisement during Christmas, upsetting trick

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it, so one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, upsetting tips a word over so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas
ad is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A seasonal TV commercial plays an unkind practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The festive word is turned upside down first, then the advertisement goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive them, coaxing them into believing something false.

clue.text: One may be prepared for an early board meeting

definitions.text: One may be prepared for an early board meeting

parts.words: One may be prepared for an early board meeting
parts.note: surface reading: papers got ready for directors convening first thing; setter's reading: board in its old sense of a table where meals are served, laid for the first meal of the day

explanation.walkthrough: The business language points to a boardroom; board here means a dining table, as in 'bed and board', and it is set before the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This piece of furniture is laid each morning for the first meal of the day, when a household gathers round it.

clue.text: Change of direction gets reader put out

indicators.note: something put out is disordered or thrown into confusion, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader is annoyed when a story suddenly takes a new course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as upset; only 'out' is the signal, and 'put' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A departure is a deviation from a set course or plan, a new direction.

clue.text: Hilary and others making stipulations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Hilary is a term at Oxford and in the English law courts, alongside Michaelmas and Trinity
second meaning: the conditions of an agreement

explanation.surface: Hilary and her friends are laying down conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person; it is the name of the spring academic period at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic sessions are terms, and the conditions set out in a contract are also its terms.

clue.text: Vehicle runs into pussy

indicators.note: one thing running into another ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A car or van knocks down somebody's cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart is a simple wheeled vehicle, often pulled by a horse.

clue.text: A strange girl offering a plant

parts.note: taken as written
rum is British slang for odd or strange
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An odd young woman hands over a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a word of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a plant with a large white funnel-shaped spathe, also called the calla.

clue.text: There is possibly nothing in that conjecture

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so this piece goes within the reshuffled letters
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A sceptic suspects a theory may hold nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to speculate or form ideas without proof, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: The hopeless imp, terrible as an evil spirit

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are wrecked and reformed

parts.note: all fourteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A useless little imp is described as a fearsome demon.
explanation.walkthrough: An imp is a small devil, so the surface itself belongs to the answer's world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the devil to whom Faust sells his soul in the legend.

clue.text: Wise person following university's established practice

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the wise person is placed behind the university in the answer

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
a sage is a wise person

explanation.surface: A wise academic sticks to the time-honoured customs of their university.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way something is habitually done.

clue.text: Harry? In essence, delightful!

parts.note: per se is Latin for 'by itself', in essence or intrinsically
cute means charming or delightful

explanation.surface: Someone gushes that a person called Harry is essentially delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to pester; PER SE plus CUTE gives PERSECUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, which is to hound or torment someone.

clue.text: Terrible person, but a live wire?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an outrageously badly behaved person, informally
second meaning: a wire carrying current gives anyone touching it a jolt

explanation.surface: Someone awful, yet full of energy and fun.
explanation.walkthrough: A live wire normally means an energetic person; here it is read literally as an electrified wire, the thing that gives shocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A shocker is slang for a dreadful person, and literally anything that delivers an electric shock.

clue.text: Student in the sun outside church

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps round it, so these letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: solar means of or from the sun
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An undergraduate sunbathes outside the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets the student lying in the sunshine; 'in' only joins definition to wordplay, and 'the sun' must be turned into its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a student, especially one holding a scholarship.

clue.text: Opportunities for bargains? Little Janet gets to use salary stupidly

parts.note: Jan is a short form of the name Janet

indicators.note: something done stupidly is done without sense or order, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Young Janet is allowed to fritter away her wages on foolish buys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' shortens the name rather than describing a child. The January sales are Britain's big post-Christmas discount season.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops slash prices in the January sales, so they are a prime chance to pick up goods cheaply.

clue.text: Good example of English style in register

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it, so these pieces sit inside the last word's letters

parts.note: a roll is an official list or register
E is the abbreviation for English
mode means style or fashion

explanation.surface: A grammar teacher cites a model of good English register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Register' is a language word in the surface, but here it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look to as a good example to copy.

clue.text: Stands taking most cash in special show

indicators.note: letters put on a special show are presented in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The stalls at a gala event rake in nearly all the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' tempts a solver to cut 'cash' short, but both words are whole fodder. Stands here is the verb meaning tolerates.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it, so stomachs means puts up with.

clue.text: Panic about nearest and dearest getting cosmetic treatment

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: a scare is a panic
one's nearest and dearest are one's family, one's kin

explanation.surface: Panic in the family over a beauty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Skincare is the practice of looking after the skin with creams and similar cosmetic routines.

clue.text: Arrange to rent one level of building maybe for dance

definitions.text: Arrange to rent one level of building maybe
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: to take a storey of a building as a tenant
second meaning: the idiom for getting up to dance

explanation.surface: Someone books a whole storey of a building to hold a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally, TAKE meaning rent and THE FLOOR one storey; the idiom also means to step out onto the dance floor, or to rise to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who take the floor go out onto the dancing area and begin to dance.

clue.text: Travel with endless enchantment — get a good book!

indicators.note: something endless has had its end taken away, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to go is to travel
a spell is an enchantment

explanation.surface: A holiday tip: go somewhere magical and take a decent novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Book is the Bible, and each of its four Gospels is a book within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospel is one of the four books of the New Testament telling the life of Jesus.

clue.text: Time to get a hundred into American state bureau

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: something put into another goes inside it, so this letter sits within the state's letters

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An official office in America decides it is time to hit a century.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is an office or bureau providing a particular service, often for a government.

clue.text: Roof fellow constructed with semi-precious stone

parts.note: a fellow is a man
sard is a reddish-brown semi-precious stone, a kind of chalcedony

explanation.surface: A roofer builds a top for a house set with gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansard is a type of roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steep.

clue.text: Channel in desert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long narrow trench for water
second meaning, a verb: to abandon or dump

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a watercourse in a desert, but desert is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditch is a dug drainage trench, and to ditch someone is to abandon them.

clue.text: Game John's written about in periodical

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the next piece

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical

indicators.note: a name written about is set down every which way, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine runs a feature on a game John has written.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled name sits between MA and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahjong is a Chinese game for four players using engraved tiles.

clue.text: Fellow given sanction, man in special headgear

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
to let is to allow or sanction
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A chap gets permission to wear a fancy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in special headgear' looks like a single phrase; man is only a name, and the definition is the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or garland for the head, so someone chapleted is wearing one.

clue.text: A flowering plant some pull up insanely

indicators.note: some means a part of what follows, so the letters sit inside the run of words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A gardener's flower that some people pull up for no sane reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' sounds like a reversal signal, but the plant reads forwards inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers.

clue.text: Measure to get bits from waste products

indicators.note: bits taken from words are fragments of them, so the letters lie within the phrase

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An instruction for sampling what is left in rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken to achieve something, as in taking steps.

clue.text: Nativity event at school? It's easy to organise!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a play put on by schoolchildren at Christmas
second meaning: the idiom for a task that is no trouble

explanation.surface: A teacher insists the school Christmas show will be no trouble to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: British primary schools traditionally stage a nativity play at Christmas, acted by the children; read as one phrase it is the idiom for anything effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is child's play is so simple that even a youngster could manage it.
